title: Rav Achi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Bava Metzia 90b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.90b.4), where he disagrees with Rav Ashi; the reading of Dikdukei Soferim (דק"ס) there is Rav Itai, whom Hyman identifies as Rav Asi the Third, a colleague of Rav Ashi. Likewise in [Eruvin 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.10a.12), "Rav Achi thought, before Rav Yosef, to say" — the reading of Dikdukei Soferim is "Rav Itai thought, before Rav Ashi." This is what Sefer Yuchasin brought as Rav Ati in the time of Rav Ashi, whom Hyman identifies as the last Rav Asi. And in Dikdukei Soferim you will find several times the name Rabbi Ati or Itai in place of Rabbi Asi.[^1]

notes.text: The consulted Bava Metzia has Rav Achi opposite Rav Ashi, and Eruvin has Rav Achi before Rav Yosef. [Heilprin’s Achi entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=368&lang=en) records both readings and raises a chronological difficulty. Compare [Hyman’s Rav Athi entry](https://www.girsology.com/toledot.html?entry=h-d5d9554b20b20d28&lang=en) for his interpretation of the reported Dikdukei Soferim variants.
